aggregates.claim: A finite ledger over the exact current collected suite, with every execution ID, primary requirement, input/profile fingerprint, current adjudication, declared phase and evidence class bound into the inventory review. Inventory adjudication is distinct from case approval: explicit current needs-oracle or disputed members remain listed, unapproved and ineligible for qualified passes. Unreviewed, stale or falsely labelled reference evidence cannot be silently adopted. Declared-valid runtime effects, other effects, positive admission controls, undefined-result contexts and invalid-input diagnostics have separate populations. Actual observations are joined by exact ID and compiler configuration without adding an execution or attributing a canonical case to this requirement.
aggregates.limitation: Observational infrastructure only: S4.2-001's facet remains pending until the source/requirement census, complete conforming fixture/oracle inventory and separate processor/dependency qualifications are independently established. No finite run proves the universal processor obligation. A filtered invocation retains all unselected members in its denominator. XFAILs remain failures; skips, unsupported modes, missing profiles, unavailable launchers, unexecuted run effects and provisional observations cannot become qualified passes. A compile/link admission is not execution of an interpretation, and a context-only run is not an assertion about an undefined value. Resource failures do not establish permitted size/complexity limits. Compiler headers, companions, launchers and profile observations describe the selected interface, not ABI certification or universal portability. Paragraphs 7-8 are recommendations, not manufactured mandatory documentation requirements.

review.rationale: Renewal of the whole-suite execution inventory after the WHERE masking FIXTURE packet in doc/source_audits/batch_120.json. The member count moves from 2102 to 2124 because this packet adds twenty-two executable cases; authored_facets moves 1807 to 1829, and the full suite is 978 tests, OK. All 2047 raw reviews, 263 catalogues, 22 links, R402 and the b153c75b baseline remain exact at the time of this renewal. Twenty-two facets of 10.2.3.2 are established across S10.2.3.2-001, -004, -005, -006, -007, -008 and -012, covering top-level control and pending masks, masked ELSEWHERE, final ELSEWHERE, END WHERE restoration, nested constructs, nested statements, and selected and unselected element values. All 34 facets of 10.2.3.1 remain pending as syntax, source-control or diagnostic constraints, and 19 of 10.2.3.2 remain pending because a conforming program cannot count mask evaluations or observe skipped evaluation, and because the p13 and p14 facets are permissions rather than required effects. Non-vacuity was proved by mutation rather than inspection: ignoring the mask failed 22 of 22, inverting it failed 22 of 22, perturbing an expected element failed 22 of 22, a masked ELSEWHERE using its own mask alone failed 6 of 6, treating a nested construct as a statement failed 5 of 5, treating a nested statement as a construct failed 1 of 1, and suppressing END WHERE restoration failed 3 of 3. No MERGE, PACK, COUNT, UNPACK, ALL or ANY is used as an oracle; expected arrays are hand-written literals; masks are neither all-true nor all-false; and sentinels are distinct from every value any branch could write. Under gfortran 16.1.0 with -std=f2023 all 22 pass with agreement on 22 of 22. Under the frozen LFortran 0.65.0-411-ga0afaa840b-dirty, 19 of 22 pass and three fail, all S10.2.3.2-006 restoration cases. The reviewer hand-derived the required final arrays for all three from the source and confirmed they match the fixtures, so these are genuine LFortran defects and not false fixtures: LFortran computes stale-sentinel values for the post-construct elemental update, a sequencing and stale-right-hand-side defect. Compiler consensus is not an oracle and gfortran agreement alone would not have settled this; the hand derivation did. Those three failures are being recorded as XFAILs against the frozen target in a separate execution operation, as the protocol requires, and no fixture was weakened or worked around. This is the first baseline change in this session, after 35 batches in which tests/expected_failures.txt was byte-identical. All remaining pending facets, unresolved units, the retained needs-oracle real-BOZ block and every global gate remain open.
